title: Improving the care for people affected by Long/Post-COVID (LCovB) – Interviews
summary:
The health-related and psychosocial impacts of Long or Post-COVID conditions are considerable for both affected individuals and their relatives. Despite increasing research efforts, the actual prevalence remains unclear. Estimates suggest that approximately 5–15% of all individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 develop a Long or Post-COVID syndrome. The current care situation of those affected is often inadequate, despite the availability of initial clinical guidelines. Especially in outpatient care, many healthcare providers report high levels of strain and uncertainty when dealing with the complex symptomatology.
Through comprehensive data collection, the Innovation Fund project “Improving the care for people affected by Long/Post-COVID (LCovB)” aims to determine the prevalence of physician-diagnosed Post-COVID illness and the care situation of individuals affected by Long/Post-COVID, to identify care gaps and barriers, and to derive key points for optimizing healthcare provision particularly in outpatient care for individuals who are severely and chronically ill. The project is supported by an expert panel consisting of professionals and people with lived experience. 
The overall project is divided into four study modules. 
In study module 3, interviews with 15 individuals affected by post-COVID are to be conducted in order to examine their care situation in more detail. The aim is to gain a better understanding of how those affected experience their care, what challenges and support needs they perceive, and what possibilities for improvement they identify.
The results of the study modules will be consolidated. Based on this synthesis, practice-oriented recommendations for healthcare provision will be developed in collaboration with the expert panel.

interventions.name:
This is a non-interventional study. 
Qualitative interviews will be conducted with 15 individuals who are affected by Post-COVID at the time of the interview.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient German language skills to participate in an interview
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of written informed consent
